title: Adonijah at the Horns of the Altar
reflectionText: Adonijah’s guests heard that Solomon was made king; they were afraid and went their way. Adonijah, afraid because of Solomon, hung onto the horns of the altar. Solomon said, “If he shows himself a worthy man, not a hair of his shall fall to the earth,” then, “Go to your house.” What are you holding onto in fear today?
editorialNotes: Packet 035 initial writer output. Short-only owner plan. The retelling remains within 1 Kings 1:41-53 and follows 1633 (1 Kings 1:28-40). Verse 41’s “heard it” is rendered “heard the noise” in both lanes, using the verse’s own noun, and verse 53’s “He came”/“And he came” names Adonijah. Jonathan’s report in verses 43-48 is one quotation, with the servants’ blessing and David’s words as inner quotations. It keeps WEB “worthy man”/“good news”/“hung onto”/“swear to me first”/kill and KJV “valiant man”/“good tidings”/“caught hold on”/“swear unto me to day”/slay in their own lanes, and ends with Solomon sending Adonijah to his house in verse 53.
